t: This is Mulberry House, number 36 Smith Square, in the City of Westminster. It was built in 1911 as a private house for Reginald McKenna, a Liberal politician who served as Home Secretary and Chancellor of the Exchequer, and later chaired the Midland Bank. The architect was Edwin Lutyens. In 1930 the house was bought by Henry Mond, Lord Melchett, who had the interior remodelled by Darcy Braddell with painters and sculptors, creating what has been described as one of the most important Art Deco interiors in London. It is a private residence again today.
